newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures cut gains late, end firm.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures cut gains late, end firm.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures cut gains during the final hour but still ended firmer.
Traders complained about the lack of business during the afternoon, as values floated back down from midday peaks on scanty order flows that resulted in low estimated volumes.
Yen and mark volume was estimated at 15,400 and 14,200, respectively, while some 6100 December sterling changed hands.

"Boring," was how one options floor broker at the International Monetary Market summed up the afternoon. "Everything just drifted off. Dollar/yen vols (volatilities) spent the day softening on no trade."
"(Trade was like) watching paint dry. There was nothing going on," added another floor broker. "Maybe with the numbers this week we'll get something going."

The market faces an impressive lineup of U.S. economic data this week, starting with Tuesday's third-quarter employment cost index, seen rising 0.8 percent, and October consumer confidence index, forecast falling to 110.6.

More critical economic information will be released later in the week, including the Federal Reserve's Beige Book, October U.S. employment report and both the Chicago and national October purchasing managers' surveys.

Morning activity focused on crosses and technicals, with yen slumping sharply under weight of its own economic, political and technical vulnerabilities rather than because of the dollar's especial vigor, traders agreed.
"It's yen weakness, not dollar strength," said one analyst.
December yen futures hovered just above a new contract low at $0.008800, which it hit overnight in electronic trading.
The Asian unit's decline helped hoist nearby sterling to another new contract high, this at $1.6132, and tugged the mark upward as well.

Yen drifted back off again but managed to hold above interim support near $0.008793, about 114.50 spot. Key support stood at $0.008755, or 115.00 spot, with resistance lurking at $0.008831 or the 114.00 level the dollar hurdled overseas.
The Canadian dollar dipped briefly after the Bank of Canada cut its key bank rate 25 basis points to 3.50 percent.
Analysts said the timing of the Canadian easing, which some had expected last week, was slightly surprising.
December yen settled down $0.000061 at $0.008813, marks firmed $0.0006 to $0.6601, Swiss francs rose $0.0003 to $0.7973, and sterling rose $0.0066 to $1.6114.

The December Canadian dollar ended flat at $0.7457, Aussie dollar rose $0.0018 to $0.7906, and the Mexican peso rose $0.000750 to $0.122700. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
